newsitem.title: FRANCE: French insurance stocks in spotlight after merger.
newsitem.headline: French insurance stocks in spotlight after merger.

text.p: Shares in French insurers Axa and Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP) grabbed the spotlight on Thursday as they requoted for the first time since announcing on Tuesday they planned to merge, creating the world's second largest insurance company.

UAP shares soared at the opening, leaping 17.19 percent from their close on November 8. The stock, which closed 16.34 percent higher at 136 francs, was the biggest gainer in the market on huge volume of over 15.9 million shares.
It was by far the most heavily traded stock for the day.

Axa meanwhile closed 3.77 percent lower at 306.5 francs on volume of 4.7 million shares as investors reacted to the expected dilution of Axa share value from the merger which is set to occur through a stock swap.
Investors from all over the world were furiously buying UAP shares to take advantage of a hoped for premium if, as expected, the deal is approved by French authorities.
Dealers at the Paris bourse said action in the two shares was intense and almost impossible to keep up with.
"It's been totally, absolutely wild," said one trader. He said major international dealers, trading for their own accounts were behind a lot of the trades.
Trading in UAP and Axa lost some of its frenetic pace by midday but remained heavy.
Dealers and analysts said the heavy interest in UAP shares was a sign of international interest and approval for the deal.
In a surprising development, UAP shares were actually suspended limit-down after their surge at the open.
The SBF stock markets' association said this was because they had recalculated the value of UAP shares to take account of the terms of the planned stock swap, expected to be approved early next week.
The swap, which comprises four Axa shares and four certificates of guaranteed value for each ten UAP shares held, values UAP shares at 157 francs.

Though the certificates will not begin trading until the conclusion of the stock swap, French stock market authorities used the anticipated value of UAP shares after the swap to calculate upper and lower trading limits for Thursday's session.
Trading in shares is suspended in Paris when a stock moves ten percent in either direction from its last closing price.
Without the recalculation, UAP shares would have been suspended limit up at the open.

As it was the revaluation of the shares, which put their lower limit at 135 francs, resulted in the surprising sight of UAP shares being briefly suspended limit down, despite trading nearly 16 percent above their November 8 close at the time.
